core_obligations: Y is the scheme theoretic union of a subset of the irreducible components of X (proof lines 4812-4816), so the analysis reduces to points y of Y by component count.

Cases at a closed point y (proof lines 4817-4840): on the smooth locus Y and X agree near y and Y is smooth; a node on a unique component stays a node on Y; through a node on two components, either Y contains both (Y = X near y, node) or exactly one, in which case X has two branches at y coming from O_{Y,y} and O_{Z,y}.

The intersection (proof lines 4841-4853): in the completion kappa(y)[[u, v]]/(uv) the maps to Y and Z are the two coordinate projections, so Y  cap  Z is cut out by (u, v) = the maximal ideal, giving (2)(a) disjoint spectra of finite separable extensions and (2)(b) each intersection point is a node of X.
Smoothness (proof lines 4854-4859): the completion of O_{Y,y} is regular, hence O_{Y,y} is regular, and kappa(y)/k separable gives smoothness in a neighbourhood.
proof_roadmap: Identify Y as a union of irreducible components of the reduced curve X.
Run the case analysis at a closed point: smooth locus, node on one component, node on two components with Y containing one or both.
In the two-branch case use the completed uv/(uv) normal form to compute Y  cap  Z as the closed point defined by (u, v).
Conclude separability of the residue fields, nodality, and smoothness of Y at the intersection.
difficulty_reason: The lemma controls how nodal singularities restrict to reduced closed subschemes and their scheme-theoretic complement (statement lines 4793-4810). The proof (lines 4812-4859) is a complete case analysis over the irreducible components through each point, with the load-bearing step being the computation in the completed normal form kappa(y)[[u, v]]/(uv) where the two branches become the coordinate projections and the intersection ideal is the maximal ideal (u, v). H2: the case analysis is systematic and each case is short, with one genuine completion computation.
